reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust, piecewise-linear morphology with a dominant period of 6 points (as estimated from metadata), manifesting as sharp, symmetric V- or Λ-shaped transitions between flat plateaus. Normal behavior consists of stable baselines (near-zero median in longer windows) interrupted by single-cycle, high-amplitude excursions: a rapid descent (slope ~−2.0 to −2.5 per point over 1–2 points), a brief trough (duration 1 point), then a rapid ascent (slope ~+2.0 to +2.5) back to baseline—forming a clean, narrow dip or peak. Amplitude of these excursions ranges from ~0.7 to ~1.4 robust-standardized units (90th-percentile amplitude 0.67–1.45). Noise is negligible (roughness ≈ 0, MAD often near zero), and curvature is flat outside transitions. Baseline levels vary across segments (e.g., +0.67, 0.0, −0.34), but the *shape* of the transition—sharp, symmetric, single-cycle—is invariant. Plateaus are strictly flat (zero slope), and truncation at boundaries is acceptable when the full transition is visible. Acceptable variation includes minor baseline offset shifts and ±0.2 amplitude jitter; deviations include multi-point troughs, asymmetric slopes, residual curvature, or non-plateau post-transition drift.

reference_profiles.description: A 6-point segment showing a single linear ramp up from 0.67 to 1.34 over 1 point (slope +0.67), then flat for 4 points. No trough; only an upward step. Morphology is incomplete—lacks the characteristic V/Λ shape and appears truncated or atypical.

An 18-point (3-cycle) segment with a clean, symmetric V-dip: flat at 0.0 for ~10 points, sharp drop to −2.0 over 1 point, flat trough for 1 point, sharp rise back over 1 point, then flat again. Matches expected morphology precisely; amplitude ~2.0, slope magnitude ~2.0 per point.

Another 18-point (3-cycle) segment with identical V-dip structure: flat at 0.0, sharp drop to −1.4 over 1 point, 1-point trough, sharp rise back. Slightly smaller amplitude than ref 1 but same timing and symmetry. Very low noise (MAD=0), confirming stability.

A 30-point (5-cycle) segment showing two full Λ-peaks (up-down) separated by flat baselines, plus partial third peak. Each peak rises sharply (~+2.0/slope), peaks for 1 point, falls sharply (~−2.0), returns to baseline. Baseline level is +0.67. Confirms repeatability of motif across multiple cycles and higher baseline offset.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 1 or 2 for queries with single V-dips (especially if trough is 1 point and slopes are steep); use reference 3 for queries with repeated peaks or elevated baselines; avoid reference 0 unless query shows only a monotonic step without reversal. When query length matches 18 points, align to ref 1/2 morphology; for 30-point queries, match to ref 3’s multi-cycle pattern. Baseline offset is flexible; shape fidelity (symmetry, 1-point extremum, flat plateaus) is critical.

Whether upward-only steps (ref 0) ever occur in true normal operation, or indicate contamination or boundary artifact
